meta.title: Power Atlas — Finance, government and family networks, 1870–1935
meta.description: A compact first module built from inspectable sources. Relationships are not claims of conspiracy, control, wrongdoing or shared ideology.

fed-nyfed.title: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

fraser-pujo.title: Money Trust Investigation / Pujo Committee records
fraser-pujo.publisher: FRASER, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

nodes.name: J. P. Morgan
nodes.subtitle: Banker and financier
nodes.summary: John Pierpont Morgan became one of the central figures in late-19th- and early-20th-century American finance and industrial consolidation.

facts.label: Family background
facts.value: Son of banker Junius Spencer Morgan.

facts.label: Career path
facts.value: Worked through his father's Peabody, Morgan & Co. network before helping form Drexel, Morgan & Co., later J. P. Morgan & Co.

nodes.name: J. P. Morgan & Co.
nodes.subtitle: New York banking house
nodes.summary: The banking house led by J. P. Morgan and his partners.

nodes.name: Junius Spencer Morgan
nodes.subtitle: International banker
nodes.summary: J. P. Morgan's father and a major transatlantic banking figure associated with George Peabody's London banking house.

nodes.name: Henry P. Davison
nodes.subtitle: Morgan partner
nodes.summary: Senior Morgan partner and one of the six participants in the 1910 Jekyll Island monetary-reform meeting.

nodes.name: Paul M. Warburg
nodes.subtitle: Banker and central-banking advocate
nodes.summary: German-born banker who advocated U.S. central-banking reform, attended the Jekyll Island meeting and later served on the first Federal Reserve Board.

nodes.name: Kuhn, Loeb & Co.
nodes.subtitle: New York investment bank
nodes.summary: Investment banking house where Paul Warburg became a partner after moving to New York.

nodes.name: Jacob H. Schiff
nodes.subtitle: Kuhn, Loeb banker
nodes.summary: Prominent banker associated with Kuhn, Loeb & Co.; Pujo records also list him among National City Bank shareholders in 1912.

nodes.name: Nelson W. Aldrich
nodes.subtitle: U.S. senator
nodes.summary: Republican senator from Rhode Island, chairman of the Senate Finance Committee and leading figure in pre-Federal Reserve monetary reform.

facts.label: Party and power
facts.value: Leading Republican senator; chaired the Senate Finance Committee from 1898 to 1911.

facts.label: Monetary reform
facts.value: Sponsored the Aldrich-Vreeland Act, which established the National Monetary Commission.

nodes.name: National Monetary Commission
nodes.subtitle: Congressional commission
nodes.summary: Commission created after the Panic of 1907 to study banking and monetary reform.

nodes.name: Jekyll Island Conference
nodes.subtitle: Secret monetary-reform meeting
nodes.summary: Six men met privately in November 1910 to draft a plan for banking-system reform that later influenced the Federal Reserve framework.

nodes.name: Federal Reserve System
nodes.subtitle: U.S. central-banking system
nodes.summary: Created by the Federal Reserve Act of 1913.

nodes.name: Federal Reserve Board
nodes.subtitle: Federal Reserve governing body
nodes.summary: Original central governing board of the Federal Reserve System.

nodes.name: Woodrow Wilson
nodes.subtitle: U.S. president
nodes.summary: President of the United States from 1913 to 1921.

nodes.name: Benjamin Strong Jr.
nodes.subtitle: First governor of the New York Fed
nodes.summary: Banker who worked closely with Morgan during the Panic of 1907 and led the Federal Reserve Bank of New York from 1914 to 1928.

nodes.name: Bankers Trust Company
nodes.subtitle: New York trust company
nodes.summary: Banking institution where Benjamin Strong served as vice president and later president.

nodes.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
nodes.subtitle: Federal Reserve Bank
nodes.summary: Opened for business in November 1914 under Benjamin Strong's leadership.

nodes.name: Panic of 1907
nodes.subtitle: Banking and financial crisis
nodes.summary: A major financial panic that exposed weaknesses in the U.S. banking system and helped drive monetary-reform efforts.

nodes.name: John D. Rockefeller Sr.
nodes.subtitle: Standard Oil founder
nodes.summary: Industrialist who built Standard Oil and later devoted substantial wealth to philanthropy.

facts.label: Origins
facts.value: Born in Richford, New York; family lived in modest circumstances.

facts.label: Religion
facts.value: Active Baptist; became a church trustee at age 21.

facts.label: Standard Oil
facts.value: Organized Standard Oil in 1870 with William Rockefeller, Samuel Andrews, Henry Flagler, Stephen Harkness and others.

nodes.name: John D. Rockefeller Jr.
nodes.subtitle: Philanthropist
nodes.summary: Son of John D. Rockefeller Sr.; major philanthropist and first president of the Rockefeller Foundation.

nodes.name: Abby Aldrich Rockefeller
nodes.subtitle: Philanthropist
nodes.summary: Daughter of Senator Nelson Aldrich and wife of John D. Rockefeller Jr.; later a major patron of modern art.

nodes.name: Standard Oil Company
nodes.subtitle: Oil company and trust
nodes.summary: Oil enterprise organized in 1870 that grew into a dominant U.S. refining and petroleum business before its court-ordered breakup.

nodes.name: William Rockefeller Jr.
nodes.subtitle: Industrialist and financier
nodes.summary: Brother and business associate of John D. Rockefeller Sr.; Pujo records list him as a substantial National City Bank shareholder.

nodes.name: James Stillman
nodes.subtitle: National City Bank chairman
nodes.summary: Banker and major shareholder who chaired National City Bank.

nodes.name: Frank A. Vanderlip
nodes.subtitle: National City Bank president
nodes.summary: Banker who served as president of National City Bank and attended the Jekyll Island meeting.

nodes.name: National City Bank of New York
nodes.subtitle: Major New York bank
nodes.summary: Predecessor of today's Citibank; a major New York institution scrutinized in the Pujo Committee's investigation of concentrated financial power.

nodes.name: Money Trust Investigation
nodes.subtitle: Pujo Committee investigation
nodes.summary: Congressional investigation into concentration and control of money and credit in the United States.

nodes.name: The Rockefeller Foundation
nodes.subtitle: Philanthropic foundation
nodes.summary: Foundation established in 1913 by John D. Rockefeller with the mission of promoting human well-being.

edges.label: headed
edges.note: Morgan headed the banking house that carried his name.
edges.establishes: Morgan led J. P. Morgan & Co. during this period.
edges.doesNotEstablish: This does not imply control of every institution financed or advised by the firm.

edges.label: father of
edges.note: Junius Spencer Morgan was J. P. Morgan's father.

edges.label: senior partner at
edges.note: Davison was a senior Morgan partner.

edges.label: attended
edges.note: Davison was one of the six Jekyll Island participants.

edges.label: partner at
edges.note: Warburg joined his father-in-law's New York banking company as a partner after moving to New York.

edges.label: attended
edges.note: Warburg was one of the six participants in the 1910 Jekyll Island meeting.

edges.label: chaired
edges.note: Aldrich led the National Monetary Commission.

edges.label: led and attended
edges.note: Aldrich led the small group that met privately at Jekyll Island.

edges.label: attended
edges.note: Vanderlip attended the Jekyll Island meeting.

edges.label: plan helped lay foundation for
edges.note: Federal Reserve History describes the Jekyll Island plan as laying a foundation for the later Federal Reserve framework.
edges.establishes: There was an institutional and intellectual lineage from the Jekyll plan to later Federal Reserve legislation.
edges.doesNotEstablish: The Federal Reserve Act was not identical to the Jekyll Island plan, and Congress enacted a different final structure.

edges.label: appointed to Federal Reserve Board
edges.note: President Wilson appointed Warburg to the first Federal Reserve Board.

edges.label: member / vice governor
edges.note: Warburg served as a Board member and later vice governor.

edges.label: governing body of
edges.note: The Board served as the central governing body of the Federal Reserve System.

edges.label: vice president / president
edges.note: Strong rose through Bankers Trust and became its president in 1914.

edges.label: governor
edges.note: Strong became the first governor of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

edges.label: Reserve Bank within
edges.note: The New York Fed is one of the Federal Reserve Banks in the Federal Reserve System.

edges.label: organized private crisis response
edges.note: Morgan became a central private coordinator during the Panic of 1907.

edges.label: examined Knickerbocker Trust at Morgan's request
edges.note: Morgan asked Strong to examine Knickerbocker Trust's books during the crisis.

edges.label: helped prompt monetary-reform response
edges.note: The Panic of 1907 helped drive the reform effort that produced the National Monetary Commission.

edges.label: organized / led
edges.note: Rockefeller organized Standard Oil in 1870 and led its development.

edges.label: brother of
edges.note: William Rockefeller was John D. Rockefeller Sr.'s brother and business associate.

edges.label: co-organizer / shareholder
edges.note: Rockefeller Archive Center identifies William Rockefeller among the founders of Standard Oil.

edges.label: son of
edges.note: John D. Rockefeller Jr. was the son of John D. Rockefeller Sr.

edges.label: daughter of
edges.note: Abby Greene Aldrich was Senator Nelson Aldrich's daughter.

edges.label: married
edges.note: John D. Rockefeller Jr. and Abby Greene Aldrich married in 1901.

edges.label: established and endowed
edges.note: Rockefeller established the foundation in 1913 and supplied its first major funds.

edges.label: first president
edges.note: Rockefeller Foundation records identify John D. Rockefeller Jr. as its first president.

edges.label: chairman / major shareholder
edges.note: Pujo records identify Stillman as board chairman and the largest listed shareholder, with 47,498 shares in the 1912 schedule.
edges.establishes: Stillman held a major ownership and leadership position at National City Bank.
edges.doesNotEstablish: Share ownership alone does not establish that every bank action reflected Stillman's personal direction.

edges.label: president
edges.note: Pujo records identify Vanderlip as president of National City Bank.

edges.label: 10,000 shares listed in 1912
edges.note: The Pujo investigation's shareholder schedule lists William Rockefeller with 10,000 National City Bank shares.

edges.label: 1,750 shares listed in 1912
edges.note: The Pujo investigation's shareholder schedule lists John D. Rockefeller with 1,750 National City Bank shares.

edges.label: 15,000 shares listed in 1912
edges.note: The Pujo investigation's shareholder schedule lists J. P. Morgan & Co. with 15,000 National City Bank shares.

edges.label: 500 shares listed in 1912
edges.note: The Pujo investigation's shareholder schedule lists Jacob H. Schiff with 500 National City Bank shares.

edges.label: documented ownership and governance
edges.note: The Pujo investigation documented National City Bank's leadership and significant shareholders.
